content:
Dear Verdane Care hiring team,

I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience role. I am a third-year Computing student at Liffey Institute of Technology, with hands-on experience building React and TypeScript applications, including a full-stack project with a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL.

During my software development internship at Harbourline Media, I implemented React components and accessibility fixes for a news website. I also built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages, documented it in Storybook, and used Jest and React Testing Library for unit and component testing. In my final-year project, Tidewatch, I built an accessible web app end to end and tested it with NVDA and VoiceOver; it achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.

I am interested in bringing this experience to patient-facing features at Verdane Care. Your focus on accessible experiences and the principles “Patients first” and “Simple beats clever” resonate with the care I take to make web applications easier to use. Alongside Tidewatch, my projects include a Next.js booking site and a React frontend for a collaborative study-matching app. I have also supported around 30 first-year students in web development lab sessions.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my frontend, accessibility and project-based full-stack experience could contribute to the Patient Experience team.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, well structured, and appropriately tailored to Verdane Care. It clearly connects the candidate’s internship and Tidewatch project to accessibility, React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library. The reference to “Patients first” and “Simple beats clever” is relevant and supported by the job description. The main content limitation is that the letter does not make the candidate’s wellness-related Yoga Studio project explicit, despite that being relevant to Verdane Care’s healthcare and wellness domain. It also does not explicitly distinguish project-based full-stack experience from professional experience, although it does not falsely claim two years of professional experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-readable: it uses standard paragraphs, no problematic formatting, and includes several relevant keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js, and Firebase-related project experience through the associated CV. Its AI-screening probability is moderate rather than high because the document does not address or evidence several advertised terms, including end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, OWASP Top 10, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, health-data privacy, and 2+ years of professional experience. These are candidate-experience gaps or unsupported areas rather than formatting defects. The letter itself is also not expected to carry every technical keyword because the CV is the primary screening document.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the frontend, accessibility, React/TypeScript, project-based Node.js/Express/PostgreSQL, testing, Storybook, and user-focused aspects of the role. Tidewatch’s accessible public-facing application and the image-gallery work are particularly relevant to patient experience. The Yoga Studio booking site provides a truthful wellness connection but is currently not identified as such in the letter. The candidate has a gap against the requirement for 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience: the source material shows a four-month internship and project work. The source material also does not establish end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, OWASP Top 10 awareness, semantic HTML, responsive-layout experience, health-data privacy willingness, German/Croatian, AWS/Docker, or analytics/A-B testing. These gaps should not be presented as document defects or claimed in the letter without supporting evidence.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the third paragraph, replace “Alongside Tidewatch, my projects include a Next.js booking site and a React frontend for a collaborative study-matching app” with “Alongside Tidewatch, I built a Next.js booking site for a yoga studio, including a class timetable and booking requests, and a React frontend for a collaborative study-matching app.” This makes the candidate’s truthful wellness experience explicit and strengthens alignment with Verdane Care’s healthcare and wellness context.

I am interested in bringing this experience to patient-facing features at Verdane Care. critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and clearly tailored to the Full-Stack Engineer role. It presents relevant evidence rather than making unsupported claims, including React/TypeScript development, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility testing, Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library. The structure is easy to follow: application motivation, relevant experience, company alignment, and closing. The main content limitation is that it does not mention the candidate's Firebase Authentication experience, which could strengthen alignment with the security and authentication requirement. It also does not explicitly distinguish professional experience from academic and project experience, although it avoids falsely claiming two years of professional experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings-free letter formatting, readable paragraphs, and relevant exact keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, NVDA, VoiceOver, Next.js, and accessibility. The terminology is generally aligned with the advertisement. Screening strength is high for frontend, accessibility, testing, Storybook, Next.js, and project-based full-stack experience, but lower for the combined requirements involving 2+ years of professional experience, end-to-end testing, Git workflows, OWASP Top 10, and health-data privacy because the candidate material does not substantiate those areas. The associated CV should carry the detailed keyword coverage; this letter appropriately remains short.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with Verdane Care's patient-facing and accessibility focus. Tidewatch provides a credible example of building an accessible end-to-end application, and the yoga studio booking site gives relevant wellness and booking-domain context. Referencing “Patients first” and “Simple beats clever” is appropriately tailored and supported by the advertisement. The candidate's material shows backend experience with Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL, automated unit/component testing, Firebase Authentication, Next.js, Storybook, and wellness-related project work. Gaps remain in the stated 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, OWASP Top 10 awareness, health-data privacy experience or stated willingness to learn it, German/Croatian, AWS/Docker, and analytics/A/B testing. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting the letter.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENT:
1. In the third paragraph, replace the sentence “Alongside Tidewatch, I built a Next.js booking site for a yoga studio, including a class timetable and booking requests, and a React frontend for a collaborative study-matching app.” with: “Alongside Tidewatch, I built a Next.js booking site for a yoga studio, including a class timetable and booking requests, and developed React login screens using Firebase Authentication for a collaborative study-matching app.” This preserves the existing project examples while adding the candidate's supported authentication experience, which is directly relevant to the security fundamentals requirement.

2. In the final paragraph, change “my frontend, accessibility and project-based full-stack experience” to “my React and TypeScript frontend, accessibility, testing and project-based full-stack experience.” This uses the job's terminology more precisely and highlights testing, which is already evidenced earlier in the letter.
